resources.string: The messages shown here are marked as handled. Nothing is removed from your phone\'s own notifications, and you can undo right after.
Couldn\'t send it. Open the app to reply.
Android cuts long notifications at about 1,000 characters. Open the app to read the rest.
Xiaomi: in Settings turn on Autostart for Sende, and set its battery saver to “No restrictions”. Menu names can differ slightly on your phone.
Huawei / Honor: Settings > Battery > App launch: set Sende to “Manage manually” and switch all three options on.
Samsung: Settings > Battery > Background usage limits: take Sende out of “Sleeping apps” and add it to “Never sleeping apps”.
Oppo / Realme / OnePlus: allow Sende to run in the background and turn Auto-launch on in the battery settings.
Vivo / iQOO: Settings > Battery > Background power consumption: allow Sende to run in the background.

The only network use in this version belongs to Google Play (for supporter plans), never your messages.
Sende only reads notifications of the apps you pick, and keeps them in a private store on this phone. It never sends your messages anywhere. You can turn access off any time in Android settings.
This permanently deletes every message Sende stored on this phone and resets your channel choices. It cannot be undone.

Your phone stopped Sende in the background, so new messages are not arriving. Restart it, and let Sende run in the background in battery settings.
Android only lets an app read notifications after you allow it once. It takes about 20 seconds.
Tap \"Open access settings\". Android opens the right page.
Find Sende in the list and switch it on.
Switch is grey and won\'t move? Android locks it for apps installed outside Google Play. Open App info, tap the three dots at the top right, choose \"Allow restricted settings\", then repeat step 2.
